findings.description: Direct inspection of all five current V191 views and six pose renders: the new neutral front is less broadly faceted than V190, but the waist-to-skirt junction remains ragged, front pleats are uneven, and the side/rear panels retain sharp planar transitions. In crouch and sit the apron still leaves broad anterior thighs exposed and falls between/behind the legs. The garment silhouette and motion response remain unacceptable.

V191 front, side, three-quarter, and prone views still show angular planar folds across the bodice, a gray waist patch with unverified garment-surface ownership, and a stiff irregular waist/back transition. Bodice appearance remains unacceptable.

V191 source-bound evidence: six sewn-graph displacement smoothing iterations (neighbor blend 0.35) anchored 108 authored front-lap hem vertices and 158 shared-seam vertices, then required a global orientation-safe scale of 0.006485. Mean effective blend was 0.003921; maximum rest displacement was 0.000817 m. Distinct anterior-thigh ray hits were 45/532 crouch and 20/532 sit, below V190 (50/532 and 21/532). This geometric evidence is not fit acceptance.

nextAction: Do not tune the V191 smoothed-field blend or hem length: a global orientation-safe scale of about 0.0065 reduced mean effective blend to 0.0039 and coverage fell to 45/532 crouch and 20/532 sit. Replace free per-vertex lower-front displacement with topology-aware panel reconstruction that preserves the exact authored hem and shared seams while following thigh motion; inspect how any boundary constraint handles the front lap as one sewn surface. Keep the separately visible bodice folds and gray waist patch blocked until the source geometry/ownership is corrected. Continue to keep fit, Shape Key, Unity/VRChat, package, and release gates blocked.
